Some time later, you wake to find yourself floating in a dark space. You shudder. Is this the afterlife? Is this really all there is? Not a bright prospect... Then you realise what woke you. A gentle voice drifts towards you, faint and distant. "Dave Parker!" it whispers. "You should know that no one can escape their destiny. Fleeing it is pointless: fate always catches up with you! Go and complete the tasks you have been given. By my divine authority, I grant you an extra life, and one more chance to fulfil your destiny..." As the voice fades, everything starts spinning. You grow dizzy and fall into a deep, dreamless sleep. When you open your eyes again, you are exactly where you tried to kill yourself...

214.text: Curiosity leads you into the dense swamp. The ground is dangerously soft and slippery, but you press on until you have to admit you're hopelessly lost. Again. Furious, you fight through the wet vegetation, looking for a landmark, but all you do is go round in circles. At last, inspiration strikes: walk in a straight line! You'll reach the island's shore eventually, then follow it back to your boat. Encouraged, you push on until you reach a little clearing. To the southeast you can see the southern shore, where that strange sign stood. The one you didn't understand. "Phew, made it!" You start to crouch down for a breather, then realise with horror that you're already knee-deep in the ground! You kick frantically, but instead of getting out, you sink deeper. Like every proper adventure, "Soul Crystal" has a quicksand location. Now you know where it is! As you settle into your new career as a bog body, take comfort in the fact that your foot has just touched the remains of another unfortunate adventurer who chose the same route...

On your left, a sign reads: "Danger - quicksand! No entry! Parents are responsible for their children!" Perhaps you should save your game before exploring any farther...?

Just how right that last statement is becomes clear when you look around. The only way out is east, straight back to the zombies. They stopped chasing you for a reason: they know this bog very well. Sooner or later, it will be your grave...

half-decomposed corpse emerges from the
depths! Frozen in horror and unable to
take your eyes off the horrific
spectacle, you watch as a zombie rises
from the depths of the bog! The moment
you regain control of yourself, its
clawed claws will shoot for your throat!
You don't know how, but somehow you
throw yourself to the side again with
all your strength and thus avoid certain
death! However, you stumble during your
parade and land hard in the mud! Now the
Blackblood seems to have finally won:
while you are struggling to get back on
your feet, he hisses and hisses at you:
as he staggers towards you, his jaws
open and close with a creaking sound,
exposing his disgustingly -brown tooth
stumps...

226.text: Sorry. You had a real chance to escape with nothing worse than a fright, but you hesitated too long. The delighted zombie pulls you close and sinks its teeth into your young, tender flesh! Still, don't despair. You've fallen victim to a true gourmet. Some of your tastier parts, eyes, tongue and similar delicacies, will doubtless be taken to its store-cave and preserved. Unfortunate adventurers stray out here far too rarely to waste such a feast in one sitting...

227.text: Coming back after your last encounter was a fatal mistake. A whole pack of zombies waits to welcome you, advancing with jerky movements and fixed stares. Leading them is the one you only just escaped! This time you react much faster. You spin round and run for your life as fast as the soggy ground allows, straight into the arms of another zombie who hadn't quite caught up with the proceedings. A shame, really. You were on course for a world record! Your new acquaintance is delighted. It hasn't had fresh meat in weeks, and a diet of bog-preserved adventurers gets a bit monotonous, even for a half-rotten stomach. After saying a quick grace, it gratefully sinks its teeth into you. "Damn! Who knew those brown stumps could still be so sharp?" is your last thought before everything blurs...

228.text: As you head south out of the enchanted forest, the amulet that protected you on your way through the magical barrier snags on a dead branch. Without your noticing, it slips from your neck. You stroll cheerfully through the boundary between the two stretches of forest and emerge on the other side of the magical wall nicely browned, but unfortunately quite dead...

229.text: Walking beneath the dead trees, you suddenly feel a vicious tug at your neck! Terrified, you thrash about, trying to shake off your invisible attacker. At last it lets go, and you nearly burst into hysterical laughter. Your "attacker" was your own amulet, caught on a branch. It now dangles from the tree as if mocking you...

230.text: Well, let's call that an attempt and leave it there. It wasn't much of a success, as you discover rather painfully. Before you can slip beneath the archway, something rattles down from above. For once, let's keep this brief: stepping on the little platform triggered the portcullis, which crushed you in one almighty blow! You're dead. Yes, really. You've kicked the bucket, bitten the dust, shuffled off this mortal coil. Gone! Don't complain to us. If you'd paid attention, you might have noticed the platform beneath the gate. So having to start again is rather more your fault than ours, isn't it? What's that? You don't believe me? Well, I can't say I blame you. You have no reason to. Perhaps this will convince you...:

243.text: Years of solitude seem to have scrambled the old man's brains, but you ask what he knows about the island anyway. "The island, the island..." he muses. "If only I knew which one you meant! The island Aeneas, that divine hero, visited long ago? Ah, I've heard of an island called America, discovered by a fellow named Columbo. No, Coulomb. Rubbish, Columbos! Oh, never mind. Nobody cares anyway. Or do you mean the island we're standing on? Yes, this is an island too, believe it or not! You can tell because it's surrounded by water, and..." You roll your eyes. This advanced geography lesson is bringing back unpleasant memories of Sesame Street. You didn't understand it then, either...

244.text: With saintly patience, you give the old man's rambling another chance, though you doubt it will be any more enlightening this time. Surprisingly, he almost answers your question. "Yes, of course I know about the island! I've lived here for over ten years! Quite right to ask me. I live here, you see, and..." He falters as he notices your hands practising a variety of strangling movements, then hastily continues. "Now, you may think me mad" - you laugh hysterically - "but at midnight the rivers here flow uphill! And under a full moon, all the adventurers swallowed by the swamp over the decades rise from their watery graves and hold wild orgies! Even Zargon, the Dark Lord himself, attends to review his undead palace guard. He once made a pact with the devil, who had his soul frozen and imprisoned in a huge magical crystal..." A knowing smile spreads over the hermit's wrinkled face as he remembers those glorious parties and the many pretty zombie girls he's enjoyed them with...

246.text: Suspecting one of the unimaginative traps that infest this country, you carefully drop the poor, innocent brick onto the platform from a safe distance. The instant it lands, the enormous portcullis crashes down! Not even a rat could have darted through in time. The brick becomes a thousand convenient little pebbles. Your heart clenches and drops into your stomach. What would you look like if YOUR weight had triggered that mechanism? More to the point, who cleaned up the mess left by the adventurers before you???
